$comment: Design Contract v1. The implementable system state, written after the direction is
It is not the direction record. The direction record explains the decision: the theses,
the runner-up, the risk, the signature. This describes what was decided, in values a
script can check and a build can be compared against. A field that only restates the
Read as data by scripts/contract.mjs. `req` is required; `enum` closes the set; `of`
types the items of a list. `why` fields are prose and the validator checks only that
they are not empty, because a reason nobody can check is still better than none: it is
read by the person who is shown the page.
The role vocabulary is structural inspiration from ui-ux-pro-max (MIT), which names
primary, on_primary, secondary, accent, background, foreground, muted, border,
destructive and ring. What is NOT taken is where the values come from: that skill
matches a product category and reads a palette off a table, which gives every glazier
the same palette. Here every role points at a primitive, and every primitive comes
from a colour found in the subject's own materials.

pairMinimums.$comment: WCAG 2.2 AA. largeText is 24px, or 18.66px at 700. nonText covers focus rings, borders that carry meaning, and icons.

subject.why: one line naming what this is, so a contract read on its own is not anonymous

writtenAgainst.note: which direction record this was written from: its path and a hash, so a contract cannot outlive the direction it implements

colour.strategy.note: restrained: one accent on a neutral ground. committed: a ground that is a colour and means something. full: several colours doing separate jobs. drenched: colour is the surface, and type and structure live inside it.

colour.sources.note: Colours found in the subject's own world. Not a palette: the material they were taken from.

colour.schemes.why.note: from the use scene, not from habit. A page read on a workshop bench in daylight and a page read in a dark room at 02:00 do not owe the same answer.

colour.genericnessRisk.note: what about this palette a competitor could also arrive at, said plainly

typography.measure.note: the prose measure the page holds

layout.path.note: the primary reading or task path, in one sentence, in order

layout.leading.note: the elements that carry the argument, by selector

layout.supporting.note: what is there to support them, by selector

layout.grouping.note: what belongs with what, and what the grouping is doing

layout.rhythm.note: the spacing rhythm: a base and the steps that come off it

layout.topology.note: the structural shape in the builder's own words. Deliberately not an enum: a closed list of topologies is a template library with a different name.

layout.firstViewportObject.note: the object that owns the first screen, and its selector. look.md section 4.

layout.signature.note: the same selector the direction record names. Repeated here so the contract can be checked without opening the record.

layout.responsive.note: 375, 768 and 1440. What the layout becomes, not what it keeps. Prose, and read by a person: contract.mjs compare does not read these words. It measures a coarse geometry proxy, which is that the leading elements do not sit in the same eight-pixel position at 375 and at 1440. See v11Candidates.adaptationVocabulary for what a real validation would need.

layout.container.note: how the container behaves as the viewport grows: what stops, what keeps going, and at what width

layout.focusOrder.note: the intended DOM and focus order, by selector, in order. The order the page is read in and the order the keyboard walks it are the same order or the difference is stated.

layout.stress.note: long content, empty, error and localization. At least one, and the surface's floor decides which are owed.

layout.squint.note: the squint test, written down: with the page out of focus, what shape is left, and is that shape the argument. Not an enum and not a score.

colour.states.note: what changes in each state the surface can be in. A state that is deliberately identical to rest says so and says why; a state left out is a state nobody thought about.

validation.note: written by contract.mjs, never by hand. An absent block means nothing has been run, which is honest; a hand-written one is a fabrication.

material.note: the thing in the subject's world this colour was taken from. 'The brand' is not a material. 'Linseed putty, two weeks old' is.

token.note: the custom property name, without the leading dashes

value.note: oklch preferred: equal steps in lightness look equal, which hex does not give you

fallback.note: the rendered sRGB stand-in. The validator checks it is the same colour.

from.note: the name of the source colour this came from, or 'derived' with a reason

backdrop.note: the opaque stack behind a translucent background, back to front, by token. Required when the background primitive has alpha under 1: a colour at nine per cent has no contrast of its own, and measuring it as if it were opaque reports a ratio nobody sees.

use.note: where this pair appears, and in which state

state.note: the interactive or semantic state this pair is painted in. rest is the ordinary one; every other value is a state the page can actually be in.

distinguishableWithoutColour.note: what carries the difference when colour does not: shape, position, hatch, label

source.note: where the file comes from: self-hosted, a foundry, a system stack

axes.note: variable axes actually used, with their range

why.note: from the subject. 'It is clean' is not a reason; it is what every default says about itself.

fallback.note: the fallback stack, in order, ending in a generic family

metricCompatible.note: does the first fallback have compatible metrics, so the page does not reflow when the webfont lands

languages.note: the scripts and language coverage this page actually needs. A Danish page needs ae, oe and aa.

expected.note: what should happen, written before it is run

result.note: written after it is run. Absent is honest; wrong is not.

selector.note: checked against the rendered DOM by contract.mjs compare

becomes.note: what the layout is at this width. Not 'it stacks'.

departures.note: what is deliberately different here from the other widths, and why

from.note: what in the direction record this departs from

changes.note: what visibly changes, in the page's own terms. 'nothing, and here is why' is an answer.

carriedBy.note: what carries it besides colour: a border, a weight, a mark, a position. Colour alone fails for anyone who cannot see the difference.

comparedAgainst.note: the url compare last ran against

stateCoverage.$comment: States every surface owes a pair for, and the ones a surface owes only when it has that thing. contract.mjs checks the first list always and the second when the surface's floor asks for it.

v11Candidates.$comment: Recorded, not built. This round deliberately added no adaptation schema; these are the shapes a later version would need, written down so the gap is a decision rather than an oversight.

adaptationVocabulary.why: layout.responsive[].becomes is prose, and prose cannot be checked against a DOM. A closed vocabulary per breakpoint could be: the contract declares which kind of change happens, and compare measures that kind.

kinds.same-with-reason: nothing changes, and the contract says why that is right
kinds.reflow: the same elements, the same order, different line breaks
kinds.reorder: the same elements in a different order
kinds.collapse: several elements become one, or a control becomes a disclosure
kinds.replace: an element is exchanged for a different element that does the same job
kinds.redraw: a drawing keeps its meaning and is drawn again at its own scale, with its own annotation
kinds.scroll: the element keeps its size and gains a scroll container, announced and keyboard reachable

adaptationVocabulary.status: candidate for v1.1. Not implemented, not scheduled, and no pilot was changed for it.
